NFL Win Totals Odds

NFL Win Totals are a type of NFL Futures market in which you are betting on the total number of wins an NFL team will have for the 2026 NFL season. NFL win totals represent one of the most engaging facets of sports betting, offering fans a chance to forecast a team's performance over the entire regular season. You will decide if the team will have more or less wins than what the FanDuel Sportsbook predicts. These bets can be made throughout the season, but the odds will adjust throughout the season as injuries, transactions, and other news breaks. Once your bet is placed, your wager will be settled at the end of the season.


How To Read NFL Win Totals

NFL win totals operate on an over/under basis. In the odds listed above, you’ll see two separate numbers for each team. You’ll see a number, such as 7.5, which indicates the number of wins a team is predicted to have. With this, you can either bet over if you think they'll win 8 or more games or bet under if you think they'll win 7 or fewer games during the regular season. Preseason games, Playoff games, and Regular Season Ties do not count towards the Win Total.

The second number you see will be a three digit number with a plus (+) sign or a minus (-) sign. With a plus (+) sign, a $100 bet will payout the number following the sign. For a minus (-) sign, you have to bet the number to win $100. To make your payout calculation easier, try adding picks to your betslip and we’ll do the math for you!

Betting Team Wins Over/Unders for the 2026 NFL Season

Using strategic thinking and researching can improve your chances of winning NFL win totals bets. Consider elements such as the team's previous season record, roster changes, injury updates, the strength of their schedule, and any coaching changes. Understanding these factors can provide valuable insights into a team's potential performance and significantly influence betting decisions.

NFL Win Totals Fluctuations

For much of the season, you will still be able to be on NFL Win Totals. However, the odds aren't static and will change throughout the year due to a variety of factors such as current performance, player trades, injuries, and changes in coaching staff. Staying updated with NFL news can allow you to find the most value in your win totals odds..


NFL Win Totals FAQs


  • When is an NFL Win Total wager officially graded?

    Win-total bets are settled after the league posts its official regular-season standings. FanDuel grades the market as soon as those standings are final and any league tiebreak-procedures are complete.

  • Do playoff games count toward a team’s win total?

    No—win-total markets cover regular-season games only. Post-season results (including the expanded wild-card round) never add to, or subtract from, a team’s win tally for this wager.

  • How are ties handled in Win Total bets?

    For settlement purposes, every game that finishes tied counts as a loss toward the win-total. Example: a team that goes 10-6-1 is treated as 10-7.

  • Can I cash out my win-total ticket early?

    FanDuel may offer Cash Out on certain futures. Availability is never guaranteed and can be suspended at any time; if presented, the amount shown is what you’d receive (stake + profit).

  • What if my team’s game is postponed or relocated?

    Win-total markets follow the league record, so a postponement or neutral-site switch has no direct effect. Once the NFL labels the game complete (even at a new date or venue), the outcome feeds straight into your bet.

Any favorite’s point spread is displayed with a “minus” symbol next to a whole number or a halved fraction, such as (-6) or (-6.5). Bettors picking the favorite “against the spread” must hope that the team wins by more than 6 points – a 1 through 6-point victory or a straight-up loss loses the wager. An underdog’s point spread is displayed with a “+” symbol, indicating the number of points “spotted” to the team before the Super Bowl kicks off. Underdog point-spread gamblers are hoping that the NFL team will “cover” by winning by any amount or losing by any amount smaller than the betting line. If the underdog’s point spread is (+6) and the team loses by 5 points, the bettors still win the payout.

If a game finishes with the favorites winning by the exact line margin shown on the point spread, bets are returned in an outcome known as a “push.”


Reading Super Bowl Moneyline Odds

Moneyline odds promise a % payoff when a sports bettor's chosen team wins the game straight-up. A favorite’s moneyline NFL odds are denoted with a “-“ as in (-200). For instance, (-150) Super Bowl odds mean that for every $150 wagered on a team, the house will pay out $100 if that team wins. (-200) odds stand for $100 payoff on every $200 wagered at the betting book. On the underdog side, moneyline odds represent the amount paid out on won $100 bets if the team surprises.
